evidence: code/vicrop.py uses a frozen pretrained CLIP (open_clip ViT-B/16, laion2B). No parameters are updated; relevancy is obtained by a forward+backward through frozen weights.

claim: The method is task-guided (the crop depends on the question text).
evidence: VicropModel.relevancy backpropagates the cosine similarity between the visual feature and the question/query text feature; the resulting relevancy map and bbox change with the text. See per_demo_predictions.json: T0..T2 share demo1.png but produce different bboxes (387,235,783,533) / (95,181,637,642) / (0,126,637,533).

claim: ViCrop crops a single ROI by thresholding the relevancy and taking the largest connected component with margin.
evidence: code/vicrop.py:relevancy_to_bbox uses gaussian smoothing, threshold quantile, scipy.ndimage.label, and largest CC selection.

claim: ViCrop integrates global and cropped views.
evidence: vicrop_predict ensembles softmax(sims_global) and softmax(sims_crop) with weight w_crop. main_results.json reports vicrop_global_only / vicrop_crop_only / vicrop_ensemble.

claim: Task-guided crops are better than naive crops on the same backbone.
evidence: baseline_comparison.png and outputs/main_results.json: ViCrop (50%) ties with no-crop and uniform-tile (50%) and beats center-crop (33.3%) and random-crop (33.3%). Crucially, on T4 (far-left magenta tulips) ViCrop is correct while center-crop and random-crop are both wrong.

claim: The relevancy map localises task-relevant content.
evidence: report/images/relevancy_heatmaps.png — Chefer relevancy hot-spots align with police officers (T1), with the DAVIVIENDA sign / shop area (T2), with the right-edge magenta tulip cluster (T4), etc. The bbox extracted from the largest CC is shown in cyan and is the same region.

claim: Ensemble weight w_crop controls the global/local trade-off.
evidence: outputs/ablations.json + ablation_threshold.png: increasing w_crop monotonically lowers mean P(correct option) from 0.413 (w=0, global only) to 0.301 (w=1, crop only); a non-trivial threshold (0.65–0.75) gives the best ROI.

claim: When the question is about a small or off-centre object, ViCrop's crop is the only configuration that gets it right.
evidence: T4 (far-left magenta tulip): center-crop predicts 'red' (wrong), random-crop predicts 'red' (wrong), ViCrop crop and ensemble predict 'magenta' (correct).

claim: Limitations: with a CLIP backbone the cropping mechanism inherits CLIP's weaknesses on very fine-grained text (license-plate characters) and on tightly mixed colour clusters.
evidence: T0 (plate first letter) and T3/T5 (mixed-colour tulip clusters): the relevancy correctly localises the silver car / right-edge cluster but CLIP's option scoring still fails. This is the OCR/colour-mixture weakness of CLIP itself, not of the cropping mechanism — exactly the regime LLaVA-1.5 (which has a language decoder) recovers in the original paper.
